chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Chess is gambling (maysir), and backgammon (nard) is gambling (maysir).

key_terms.مَيْسِرٌ: Gambling (a specific form of game of chance)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia Islamic ruling on chess and backgammon?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) equates chess (al-shatranj) and backgammon (al-nard) with maysir (gambling), a ruling that has been central to Shia jurisprudence regarding games of chance. This classification underscores the prohibition not merely on the act of wagering, but on the inherent nature of these games as distractions from spiritual duties and sources of social discord, as highlighted in the broader context of Surah Al-Ma'idah.
